newsitem.title: FRANCE: Giat France made 530 mln Ffr oper loss in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Giat France made 530 mln Ffr oper loss in 1996.

text.p: State-owned arms maker Giat Industries said its French activities made a provisional operating loss of 530 million francs ($91.1 million) in 1996, on turnover up 13 percent at 6.1 billion francs.

Giat reported a group operating loss of 1.7 billion francs in 1995, on revenues of 5.4 billion. It made a net loss of 10 billion francs due to provisions for a weak dollar hedging position and restructuring charges.

Company chairman Jacques Loppion told reporters on Thursday that the 1996 results excluded the operations of its FN Herstal small arms subsidiary and until uncertainties at the Belgian unit were settled, last year's accounts could not be closed.
He said he expected to sell Herstal to the parent company of the U.S. Colt company by the end of the year or put it into creditor protection.

Herstal, which makes Browning pistols and Winchester rifles, employs 3,000 staff. Its revenues fell to 13 billion Belgian francs in 1996 from 16 billion in 1995 and made heavy losses in 1996, Loppion said.

Giat will enter three-way talks in the next few weeks between Colt and the Walloon regional government, which owns eight percent of Herstal and holds a veto, aimed at getting a sale agreement signed in the next few months.

The improvement in Giat France's operating result was due to the rise in the dollar, 300 million francs in cost savings as part of its restructuring plan, and progress in offset programmes with the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Loppion said.
Giat also recovered 900 million francs in provisions as it delivered tanks to the UAE in the course of the year.

Giat's financial problems mainly stem from the $3.6 billion sale of 436 Leclerc battle tanks to the UAE in 1993. It took out cover for a dollar which it expected to rise. Instead, depreciation in the U.S. unit forced it into heavy losses.
The French company also expects to meet between 30 and 50 percent of its industrial offset requirements as part of its UAE tank sale. Giat also hopes to sell the Leclerc to Saudi Arabia.
The new French defence minister, Alain Richard, said in a separate briefing that Giat was in a "critical situation." But he said Giat would continue to function.

The 1996 operating loss was smaller than the forecast 820 million loss in its restructuring plan, which is aimed at bringing the group into operating breakeven by the end of 1998, Loppion said. The 1996 net position was unchanged.

Giat received a 3.7 billion franc capital injection from the government in 1996 to cover the equity consumed by financial losses in the previous years. That money has been used to fund its working capital needs and the company needs a fresh capital boost. Loppion declined to say how much.
The company expects to shed 700 more jobs by the end of 1998, on top of the equivalent of the 2,000 already lost through shorter working hours and departures through early retirement.
Giat also has to renegotiate its contract to deliver 406 tanks to the French army, as part of the restructuring plan, Loppion said. ($ = 5.818 French Francs)
